src/hook.js · src/track.js"] B["#120 spend from the transcript
src/stats.js"] C["#121 docs: what each profile reports
README.md · docs/harnesses.md"] R["#115 verify + synthesize"] C --> A C --> B R --> C ``` Arrows point from a task to what blocks it. | task | blocked by | paths | why it is its own PR | |---|---|---|---| | #119 | — | `src/hook.js`, `src/track.js`, `test/session.test.js` | the hook keys on `KB_TASK`; nothing in stats changes | | #120 | — | `src/stats.js`, `test/stats.test.js` | cold nodes already carry `transcript_path`, so this needs nothing from #119 | | #121 | #119, #120 | `README.md`, `docs/harnesses.md` | can only describe what the two actually shipped | | #115 | #121 | — | the end-to-end run on a real track, plus whatever seam the three PRs leave | Invariants: - **#119 and #120 are independent and path-disjoint**, so the dispatcher runs them at once. The tempting dependency — "stats needs the session fields" — is false: cold-node attempts already carry `transcript_path`, and #119 only widens *which* attempts have it. Adding the edge would have cost wall-clock and bought nothing. - **The root is blocked by the only leaf**, #121. Nothing is blocked by the root. - **The shared decision is written into both bodies that depend on it**: `SESSION_FIELDS` and `sessionUpdate` keep their shape. #119 owns them and is told not to move them; #120 is told to read them and not to change them. Neither worker can see the other's body. - **`test/` is deliberately not a path on any child.** #112, #113 and #116 on this board all claim `test/`, which makes three unrelated cards mutually overlapping under the `path_overlap` guard. Naming the specific test file keeps siblings parallel. Not run as a track: #119 and #120 are genuinely parallel, which node dispatch exploits and a single track session would not. Known hazard recorded for the root's verify pass: `hkb adopt` leaves the previous `kb:agent:*` label (#113), so a track adopted before that lands silently resolves to `claude` and runs as node dispatch. `hkb dispatch --dry-run` reporting `tracks 0/0` is the only symptom.

residual_risk: CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID and $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/state.json (sessionId, linkScanPath) are Claude Code's own local state, not a documented contract — verified on this host with 2.1.250. A format change yields null and today's message, never a wrong number, but the transcript answer would quietly disappear for claude-bg again. `hkb show <n>` printing a session line is the one-command check.

The Stop hook's worktree fallback also makes the nudge live for any session sitting in a kb-<n>-<k> checkout — including an operator who opens one to take a running card over. They get the nudge twice and then it stops. Recording is safe there (the marker and sessionUpdate make it record-once), and a finished card returns 0 before nudging.

An attempt that never reaches a terminal verb (crashed, timed_out, protocol_violation) still records nothing on a claude-bg profile. The dispatcher's reap path already holds the job id and could stamp it from the same readJobState it calls, but src/dispatch.js was outside this task's paths. results.summary:
The three children built the chain that prices a `claude-bg` board; verifying it end to end showed the
chain has no input on the profile it was built for, and that is what this task fixed.

## The seam (#125, and it was #115's own goal)

The dispatcher exports `KB_TASK`/`KB_ATTEMPT` on the launch, but `claude --bg` only asks Claude Code's
session daemon to start an agent and exits — the daemon was started long before, with an environment of
its own. Confirmed from inside this live worker: `process.env.KB_TASK` is undefined. So `stopHook`
returned 0 on its first line, no nudge ever fired, no `session_id` was ever written, and #119's per-node
identity and #120's transcript pricing had nothing to read. `hkb stats --since all` said "69 worker
attempts priced nothing at all"; the three that were priced date from when `claude` was a `-p` profile.

## What now records a session, and why it is the terminal verb

Two things a background session does have, neither an API call, both already conventions here:

- **which attempt it is** — its checkout. `whichAttempt` (src/hook.js) takes `KB_TASK` first and falls
  back to the `kb-<n>-<k>` the launch names, which is already how the tick identifies a running job
  (`matchJobByWorktree`). One basename, only when the environment is silent, so the Stop hook still
  returns before it reads stdin in an ordinary session. The two-nudge enforcement comes back with it.
- **which session it is** — `CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID`, and for a background agent the job record under
  `$CLAUDE_JOB_DIR`, which also names the transcript on disk. `currentSession` (src/jobs.js), beside the
  `readJobState` the dispatcher already uses. A resumed job whose record names another session yields
  only the id, never someone else's transcript.

The recording is done by the **terminal verb**, not the hook — `sessionForAttempt` (src/hook.js) called
from `finishAttempt` (src/lifecycle.js). It is the one thing every worker runs, it is already writing
that attempt row (so it costs nothing), and it does not depend on a harness firing hooks at all. It
stamps only an attempt this session actually ran — its own, or a node it claimed in-session — so an
operator finishing a card by hand and the dispatcher writing off a dead attempt record nothing. That
rule is also what gives a track its per-node identity: the runner finishes each node from inside its own
session, so each node's row carries the runner's transcript, which #126's per-file reader counts once.

`preToolHook` stays gated on `KB_TASK` alone, deliberately: a checkout name says which *task* a session
is, never which *profile* launched it, and that policy with no profile would deny a worker `npm test`.

## Numbers I actually saw

This attempt is the proof: a `claude-bg` worker with no `KB_TASK`, whose row carried nothing. Rendered
through `computeStats`/`formatStats` against the real board with this session's real 52-turn transcript:

```
spend      $9.02 reported · on 3 of 74 worker attempts
           ~$6.64 estimated on top, for 1 worker attempt priced from their transcripts — an estimate, not a reported cost
           70 worker attempts priced nothing at all — the real total is higher
usage      52 turns · in 104 · out 68k · cache 216k written / 7.2M read  (1 transcript)
```

`total_usd` stays 9.0178 (reported money only); the estimate is `estimated_usd` 6.6449 and always carries
the tilde and the word. With no `stats.rates` the same board prints the usage line and the hint, `basis`
`usage`. A track of three nodes naming one real transcript: `~$6.80` once, not three times,
`attempts_shared_session: 2`, `attempts_missing_cost: 0` — #126's fix holds now that node rows really do
share a transcript. The verb carrying this summary is the one that records this attempt's session, so
`hkb show 115` prints a `session …` line and a `claude --resume` from here on.

## One silence closed in stats

A board with no ended attempt printed no `spend` line at all — a blank where the spend line belongs reads
like a failure. It now says there was nothing to price. The other degraded paths already answered with a
message and never an error, and I checked each: an attempt with no transcript, a `transcript_path` not on
this disk, an empty file, and a path that is a directory.

## Docs and wiki

`docs/harnesses.md` — "When a profile that should report tokens reports none", written by #121 to
describe #125 as an open gap, is replaced by how the recording works, plus what still records nothing
(an attempt that never reaches a terminal verb: crashed, timed_out, protocol_violation). README's profile
paragraph and stop-nudge row follow. The wiki's `architecture/overview` claimed a worker is "pointed at
one card with `KB_TASK` set", which was never true for the default profile; it now carries the asymmetry
and both answers, with `src/jobs.js` in `covers`, a `Transcript` glossary line and a `log.md` entry.

## For the next worker

#125 is fixed by this PR and should be closed with it — it is not linked as a blocker of #115, so close
it by hand. Its second ask is not done: `hkb doctor` still cannot say "the Stop hook is inert for this
profile here", which is now a much narrower question (does this harness fire hooks at all?) and worth its
own card. Two attempts on this board are still open-ended holes by design: an attempt that crashes or
times out never runs a verb, so it records nothing — the dispatcher's reap path has the job id and could
stamp it from the same `readJobState` it already calls, in `src/dispatch.js`, which was outside this
task's paths.
